text: But by moving it into the Schedule, it allows us to look at every individual.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Today, when detainees come in, we actually do a risk analysis.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Are you likely to be high-risk, medium-risk or low-risk?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if you are low-risk, can we do all these things to make sure that you do not become a permanent feature of the system?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, likewise, we want to do that with the PSO supervisees.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We want to structure it such that we have the power to impose those sorts of tailored conditions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And in my mind, the sooner the better we move in line with everything else.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I am just trying to understand, as a follow-up to the clarification just now on the proposed system for the Judges to chair the Advisory Committee, I know the Minister mentioned tradeoffs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: But I do not think he quite explained why did he shift from one position to the other.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The way I look at it is that it could be the same one or two Judges sitting there, making a decision either in their capacity as Supreme Court Judges, or as chair of the advisory committee.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: They could be using the same legal reasoning and all that.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: But the Minister correctly observed that between 1989 and 1994, he had changed this position and explained that there are tradeoffs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Could the Minister explain why is one preferred to the other?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Sorry, is the Member asking me why I changed my mind between 1989 and 1994?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Yes, you explained that by 1994, you had changed your mind and that you recommended it, as what you are going to do now – that Judges chair the Advisory Committee.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, my question again is: what made you change your mind?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: What made you prefer one over the other because, as I have said, if it is the same one or two Judges sitting there using the same experience and training and making the same decision, is the Government concerned that the decision stops there – it overrules the Minister's and it ends there?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: On the other hand, in the Advisory Committee, there is a further process of presenting it to the President and the President acting on the advice of the Cabinet?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I just need to know the reason for preferring one to the other now.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Even in 1989 and 1994, I did not conflate the two because, conceptually, they are very different.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Which is why in answer to the Member's points earlier, I said what he is suggesting is quite radical – radical in the sense that, "Look, it is either an Executive process or a judicial process." So, we have to apply our minds.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is it something where you want the Minister to decide?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Or is it something that you want the Courts to decide?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If it goes to the Courts, you know the process – it has got to be through evidence; it has got to be through witnesses.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When the Court sits in review, in open, then the other side will have the right to look at all of the testimony.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You have got to give it to them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That undercuts the entire basis of the CLTPA because many of the witnesses do not want their evidence to come out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, one has to be conceptually clear which route do we want.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You cannot do any of that in a normal Court process which is why I said that the Member's suggestion really means we do away with the CLTPA.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You cannot have the cake and eat it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is either one or the other, and you are to decide which one.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It seems to me that the Minister is saying that the amendment before the House has no effect on the current legislation as it is.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: If there is no effect, then why amend something that is unnecessary?
